changes.loss:
Add a normalized timing-weighted star-edge cut penalty to the parent loss.

Change vs parent: the random-walk contrastive term is kept, and a
timing-weighted ``softplus(-graph_scores)`` term is added over the
published loss-context stars. This encourages endpoints of high-weight
timing nets to receive same-side embeddings, which the unchanged decoder
can then turn into fewer cut timing edges. Expected effect: lower
timing-weighted cut and improved TNS, with WNS roughly neutral. The
hypothesis is invalidated if paired seeds keep the same legal assignment
and timing, or if timing regresses broadly across cases and seeds.

changes.decoder:
Replace the parent reference-helper call with a custom area-targeted two-center loop.

Change vs parent: deterministic farthest-point two-center initialization,
bounded area-weighted center updates, then a final whole-supernode split by
projection rank with cumulative physical area closest to ``balance_target``.
Expected effect: move supernodes across the area-balanced boundary that the
reference helper left unchanged, improving TNS more than WNS while protected
closure repairs macro feasibility. Invalid if the returned partition is
mostly unchanged from the parent or if timed WNS/TNS regress on valid pairs.

changes.loss:
Use a timing-weighted margin attraction on graph star edges.

Change relative to the parent: keep the maintained random-walk
positive/negative log-sigmoid contrastive term, and add a normalized
timing-weighted graph penalty ``softplus(0.25 - graph_scores)``.  The
positive margin asks critical connected groups not merely to avoid a
negative dot product but to separate from the decision boundary, which
should make the area-balanced two-way decoder choose a different discrete
partition more readily than a plain zero-margin graph penalty.

Expected measurable effect: lower timing-weighted cut and improved TNS,
with a visible change in decoder labels or closure movement on at least a
subset of cells while retaining the parent contrastive behavior.

Hypothesis is invalidated if paired WNS/TNS and final labels remain at the
parent levels, or if the larger graph attraction collapses the embedding
split so that feasibility closure has to move many groups.

Add a stronger timing-weighted star-edge attraction term to the parent loss.

Change relative to the parent: keep the sampled random-walk log-sigmoid
contrastive objective unchanged, and add a normalized timing-weighted
margin attraction on the supplied timing-context star edges.  The margin
term pushes endpoints of timing-weighted connected nets toward a positive
embedding dot product, with normalization by total graph edge weight so the
graph term remains comparable across nets.

Expected measurable effect: the timing-weighted graph attraction reshapes
embeddings more strongly, so the unchanged area-balanced two-center decoder
should move at least a few supernodes across the partition boundary and
improve TNS where timing-weighted connectivity is informative.  The main
risk is a WNS regression on bp_fe-ng45.

Invalidation: if the official labels remain unchanged on most training
cells, or if the combined score does not exceed the parent, this stronger
graph-attraction mechanism is not useful.

changes.decoder:
Replace the parent's single reference_global_two_way handoff with one bounded
custom two-center loop whose assignment step is a global area-balanced sweep.

Change vs parent: instead of per-node nearest-center labeling plus whole-group
rounding, each iteration ranks nodes by the squared-distance margin to the two
area-weighted centers, cumulatively sums physical area along that ranking, and cuts
where cumulative area first reaches `balance_target * total_area`. Centers are then
refreshed from the resulting labels. Labels are oriented so the group whose
area-weighted mean embedding projects higher on the area-weighted global mean
embedding sits on the top die.

Expected measurable effect: the returned labels spend the area balance directly, so
the protected closure has almost nothing to repair and the discrete split differs
from the parent's nearest-center partition mainly in the boundary margin band,
changing final cut / timing-weighted cut and therefore TNS.

Invalidation: if the labels stay identical (up to a die swap) to the parent on most
cells, or the paired combined score does not exceed the parent's, this
balanced-sweep mechanism is not what controls the physical timing.

changes.loss:
Add a graph_weights-normalized timing-star attraction to the parent loss.

Change relative to the parent: keep the parent sampled random-walk
log-sigmoid contrastive objective unchanged, and add the weighted mean
softplus(-graph_scores) over timing-context star edges. This uses the
supplied graph weights as a normalized attraction, rather than an
unnormalized edge-count sum, to pull embeddings of timing-critical
connected supernodes together while limiting dense-net bias.
Expected measurable effect: retain the timing gains seen from stronger
star-edge attraction while reducing the bp_fe-ng45 regression, with the
reference decoder and native feasibility closure unchanged.
Invalidated if bp_fe-ng45/1001 does not improve, if the ariane133-ng45/1002
TNS gain disappears, or if labels remain unchanged while timing moves.

changes.decoder:
Refine the parent reference partition with one area-aware Lloyd correction.

Change relative to the parent: still call the trusted reference helper
exactly once with unchanged inputs to obtain a legal, area-balanced start.
Then perform exactly one non-iterative reassignment: rebuild the two
physical-area-weighted centers from the helper labels and move only
boundary nodes from the currently larger-area side to the other side when
they are geometrically closer to that other center.  No random state, no
loop, and no full label swap are introduced.

Expected measurable effect: a small number of boundary supernodes that the
reference area rounding left on the larger side but whose embeddings place
them nearer the opposite center will cross the boundary, improving final
TNS without the broad die-swap regression seen from full custom re-clustering.

Invalidation: if labels remain identical on most cells, or if the combined
score does not exceed the parent, or if a die swap appears, this refinement
is not useful.

changes.loss:
Add a moderately scaled timing-weighted star attraction to the parent loss.

Relative to the parent pure random-walk log-sigmoid objective, this keeps
the sampled positive/negative contrastive term unchanged and adds a
graph_weights-normalized softplus(-graph_scores) attraction over timing
star edges. Connected supernodes on high-weight timing nets should move
closer in embedding space, while sampled negative pairs remain separated.

Expected measurable effect: timing-sensitive groups should more often cross
the reference decoder's area-balanced boundary than in the parent, improving
the physical WNS/TNS trade-off without the large bp_fe regression seen with
a stronger unnormalized star term. This hypothesis is invalidated if most
cells keep the start assignment with no timing gain, or if timing worsens
broadly despite the normalized attraction.

Change vs parent: keep the parent's sampled log-sigmoid contrastive term,
and add two geometric terms: (1) a net-weight-normalized softplus margin on
timing-star edges to pull timing-critical connected supernodes together, and
(2) a mean-centering term that maximizes global embedding variance. The
star margin encourages graph communities to contract, while the centering
term prevents collapse and pushes the embeddings toward a two-cluster
antipodal geometry that the area-balanced two-means decoder can split.
Expected measurable effect: more discrete partition changes and improved
timing alignment on the full physical flow. Hypothesis invalidated if
assignments remain mostly identical or if WNS/TNS regress without offset.

Change vs parent: keep the sampled log-sigmoid contrastive term, and add a
net-weight-normalized softplus margin on timing-star graph edges. The edge
weights sum to each represented net's fixed timing weight, so timing-critical
nets are attracted more strongly in the learned embedding geometry.

Expected measurable effect: connected timing-critical supernodes become closer
in L2 embedding space, moving the area-balanced two-means boundary and reducing
the inter-die timing cut (especially TNS). The hypothesis is invalidated if the
paired physical evaluation shows broad regression or mostly unchanged final
assignments with no timing gain.
